So how does the amp class breakdown work? Is it a-best, b,c,d? Or is D the 'best'? I have a Fender hot rod jr and some studio monitors but I am not sure how any of that would compare.

It's not a matter of best. Class A,B,C,D is how the output transistors are configured.

Class D uses a completely different technique. It runs the transistors in a PWM mode. That is pulse width modulation mode. This mode allows the transistors to switch in a completely on and off state. Doing this is very efficient. It turns out that transistors are not very efficient in analog mode. They require a 0.6 volt bias that keeps them on all the time. This in turn, requires large heat sinks and big power supplies.

I wasn't sure how the amplifier would sound running in a switching mode like this. It turns out, with proper filtering, the amplifier works very well.

Yeah, I love the little class D amps. I built a Bluetooth Boombox from an old Tower speaker using a 200w TDA3116D2 , (2.1 50x2 +100W Bass) and I was quite impressed with the sound. Plus, it jams for 5 hours on a full charge using a Hyper Tough 20V max 1.5 AH Cordless drill battery.

Most of the larger class D amps will run comfortably on anywhere from 12-24V. When I am not using the battery, I run a Laptop power cord at 19.3 V/3.42 Amps. They will run fine on 12V, but run much much better the closer to 24V you get. Just be sure to run either a DC-DC buck step-down converter (Set at 5v) , or else an LM7805 IC for the FM/mp3 Decoder board.
